pathway.title: ELDORADO GOLD CORP /FI — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. Eldorado Gold's cash is being consumed by growth spending rather than by operations. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 it generated USD 425.7 million of operating cash flow from continuing operations but spent USD 1,210.0 million on property, plant and equipment and USD 45.9 million on capitalised interest paid, a shortfall of about USD 830.2 million before acquisition cash, dividends, buybacks and borrowings (CP-1, Calculations). Company-defined free cash flow was negative USD 654.3 million; excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay it was positive USD 202.1 million (Q3 release page:13). Mechanic: the operating mines are cash generative and the two projects absorb it, so default risk is driven by project completion, not by the operating base. Documentary Fact.

2. Liquidity has fallen but covers near-term maturities. Unrestricted cash was USD 396.8 million and the undrawn revolver USD 274.7 million at September 30, 2026, together USD 671.5 million against USD 976.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1). Principal falling due within a year is USD 141.1 million, so liquidity is about 4.8 times that amount (Calculations). Restricted cash of USD 71.9 million for the Skouries term loan reserve and the undrawn euro 30 million VAT facility are excluded. Mechanic: the cushion is adequate for scheduled repayments but not for a prolonged slip in the start-ups combined with a lower gold price. Analyst Interpretation.

3. Debt rose by USD 710.4 million to USD 1,985.4 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (carrying amount). The increase came from USD 321.6 million of revolver borrowings, USD 68.1 million from the final overrun draw on the Skouries loan, and USD 350.5 million of Foran-related debt (the Sprott facility net of its redemption option derivative asset, the equipment facility and government contributions), partly offset by repayments and movements on the Skouries project loans and the VAT facility (CP-1 debt table; Calculations). Foran itself was paid for with shares (USD 2,385.6 million of share consideration), which kept the acquisition from adding to leverage through the purchase price (CP-1A). Documentary Fact.

4. Reported leverage looks moderate only on an illustrative basis. Total debt to annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is 1.67 times and net debt to the same measure 1.34 times; neither is a trailing twelve-month figure because FY2025 EBITDA is not supplied, and the base includes Foran only from April 14, 2026 and no Skouries contribution (CP-1). Cash interest cover (Adjusted EBITDA over interest paid plus capitalised interest paid) was 11.96 times for nine months 2026 and 9.81 times for Q3 2026. These do not use the covenant definitions, so headroom against the revolver tests of at least 3.00 times interest cover and at most 3.50 times net leverage is Not calculable. The illustrative figures sit well inside those levels, which is a reading and not a compliance finding; the Company states it complied at September 30, 2026 (Q3 statements page:14). Analyst Interpretation.

5. Skouries and McIlvenna Bay execution is the pivotal risk. First concentrate was reached at Skouries on September 8, 2026 and at McIlvenna Bay in June 2026, with commercial production for both expected late in Q4 2026 (CP-1A). The Skouries project capital estimate rose from about USD 1.315 billion in the Q1 release to about USD 1.425 billion, the McIlvenna Bay estimate from USD 952 million in the Q2 release to USD 975 million, and the 2026 production outlook was cut to 425,000 to 475,000 ounces from 495,000 to 600,000 ounces. On the release's own figures, remaining Skouries project capital is about USD 46 million and accelerated operational capital about USD 104 million, with up to USD 30 million more possible (Calculations); the remaining McIlvenna Bay spend is Not calculable because spending before the acquisition date is not in the pack. Mechanic: further slippage extends the period of negative free cash flow and delays the debt reduction that management says it expects. Management Language on funding ("fully funded") is not adopted because no funding model is supplied.

6. Refinancing is concentrated and amortisation starts soon. Principal due by year after September 30, 2026 is USD 141.1 million, 142.5 million, 958.8 million, 162.4 million, 354.7 million and 258.2 million beyond year five (CP-1). The third year contains the USD 500.0 million 6.25% senior notes due September 1, 2029 and the USD 325.0 million revolver drawn to March 1, 2029, the largest bucket by a wide margin. The Skouries term loan, non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries and Hellas Gold assets, begins repaying on December 31, 2026 in 13 semi-annual instalments (Q3 statements page:13). Mechanic: if the start-ups deliver, cash flow and the equity-funded balance sheet should support refinancing; if not, the 2029 wall arrives with higher debt. Documentary Fact for the schedule, Analyst Interpretation for the refinancing reading.

7. Shareholder returns continued during the build. Dividends of USD 54.1 million and cancelled buybacks of USD 83.9 million in nine months 2026, about USD 138.0 million together, were paid while free cash flow was negative (CP-1A, Calculations). The senior notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances and the Company reports compliance. No creditor-adverse action is documented. Mechanic: these returns draw on the same liquidity that funds the projects and can be reduced by the board; they are a monitoring point, not a finding of extraction. Analyst Interpretation.

8. Earnings quality needs care. Net earnings from continuing operations were USD 426.2 million for nine months 2026 against USD 270.0 million a year earlier, but the 2025 period included a deferred tax recovery of USD 89.4 million and the 2026 effective tax rate was 37.6% against 16.8% (CP-1 Calculations). The Adjusted EBITDA measure of USD 892.0 million adds back a USD 97.6 million realised loss on gold and copper derivatives and USD 21.3 million of acquisition costs, and removes a USD 100.6 million unrealised derivative gain (Q3 release page:24). Mechanic: the realised swap loss is a real cost of the Skouries financing hedges that the adjusted figure leaves out; those swaps have expired with financial settlement (Q3 statements page:22), so the item should not recur, but the adjusted measure is higher than the unadjusted result for 2026. Documentary Fact.

runs.text: Strengths. First, the operating base earns at high gold prices: the average realised gold price was USD 4,326 per ounce in Q3 2026 against USD 3,527 a year earlier, and Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 892.0 million against USD 571.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1). Second, diversification across Turkiye, Canada and Greece with Canada now the largest segment at about 45% of nine-month revenue, and several mines at different cost levels, with Lamaque cash costs of USD 897 per ounce in Q3 2026 (CP-1A, Calculations; Analyst Interpretation). Third, an equity-funded Foran purchase that added roughly 24.7% to shares outstanding rather than debt to fund the price, and an extended and enlarged revolver of USD 600.0 million maturing March 1, 2029 (Documentary Fact). Fourth, a Skouries project loan that the notes describe as non-recourse to Eldorado Gold Corporation, which limits parent exposure to that lender if the project falls short (Documentary Fact for the description; the legal documents are not supplied, so the extent of recourse is not verified). Fifth, interest cover on cash interest of about ten to twelve times on matched bases (Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure).

Weaknesses. First, negative free cash flow and falling liquidity, with debt up USD 710.4 million in nine months (Documentary Fact). Second, cost and guidance deterioration: all-in sustaining cost guidance raised and 2026 production outlook cut, with Kisladag and Olympias weaker (Documentary Fact). Third, start-up risk and rising project capital at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, with commercial production dates still forward-looking (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Fourth, a concentrated maturity profile and the start of Skouries term loan repayments in December 2026 (Documentary Fact). Fifth, a leadership transition on September 30, 2026 during the overrun period and shareholder distributions during the build (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the credit effect). Sixth, high effective tax in 2026 and exposure to a high gold price: the earnings strength depends on a gold price the company does not control, and the pack contains no sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation; sensitivity Not supplied).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one transaction in the period is the acquisition of Foran Mining Corporation, completed on April 14, 2026 by court-approved plan of arrangement. The Q3 statements say the Company acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding common shares of Foran for 0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran share (Q3 statements page:8: "0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran common share"). Total consideration transferred was 2,394,995 (US$ thousand), of which share consideration was 2,385,625, cash 4,154, replacement option value 3,096 and the previously held equity interest 2,120; 64,668,321 shares were issued (Q3 statements pages:8, 17). The principal asset is the McIlvenna Bay project in Saskatchewan. The acquisition was therefore financed with equity, not debt, and the statements show net cash received on acquisition of 159,110 (Q3 statements page:3). Net assets acquired include property, plant and equipment of 2,696,191, goodwill of 446,181, debt assumed of 355,321 and a deferred tax liability of 501,024; the measurement is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year (Q3 statements pages:9, 10). Acquisition-related costs expensed in the nine months were 19.3 million (US$) (Q3 statements page:10). The Q1 statements disclose the completion as an event after the reporting date (Q1 statements page:22).

The debt assumed comprises the Sprott Credit Facility (a fully drawn 250 million non-revolving facility plus 44.9 million capitalised interest, maturing September 30, 2031, floating at 6.95% over the greater of three-month SOFR and 2.00%, secured by the realisable value of the acquired Foran assets and subject to a Company guarantee), the Sandvik Equipment Finance Facility (C$50.1 million outstanding, 60-month repayment) and repayable government contributions (Q3 statements pages:14, 15). Principal repayments on the Sprott facility start on June 30, 2027 at 2.65% of outstanding principal per quarter. Its terms mean the lender has a claim over the acquired assets ahead of unsecured creditors of the group on those assets, and the Company guarantee ties the facility to the parent; the pack does not include the credit agreement, so the full security and guarantee scope is Insufficient Information.

No new bond or note issue is reported in the period. New borrowing was: draws on the revolving senior secured credit facility totalling 325.0 million in the nine months (225.0 million of it in Q3 2026); the final 60.0 million euro draw on the Skouries Contingent Overrun Facility in Q2 2026; and net proceeds of 2,469 (US$ thousand) from other debt. The revolver was increased from 350 million to 450 million on May 26, 2026 through the accordion, and on August 12, 2026 amended to a 600 million limit with maturity extended to March 1, 2029 and, in the Company's words, improved pricing and covenant terms (Q3 statements page:14: "enhancing financial flexibility through improved pricing and covenant terms"). The amended covenant terms are not stated beyond the interest cover and net leverage levels in the note, so what changed is Insufficient Information. The equity commitment letter of credit under the revolver for Skouries was reduced to nil as the equity funding was completed in Q3 2026 (Q3 statements page:14), which releases revolver capacity; at September 30, 2026 the revolver availability was 274.7 million (Q3 statements page:14).

Distributions during the build: the Company initiated a quarterly dividend programme with the first payment on March 13, 2026 (Q1 release page:2), paid 54.1 million of dividends in the nine months, bought back and cancelled 2,419,992 shares for 83.9 million and bought a further 240,000 shares for 8.7 million held in trust (Q3 statements page:18), and declared a fourth quarter dividend of 0.075 per share on October 28, 2026 (Q3 statements page:18). The senior notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances and the Company states compliance (Q3 statements page:11). Mechanically, these distributions total about 138.0 million for dividends and cancelled buybacks in nine months 2026 while company-defined free cash flow was negative 654.3 million (CP-1), so they were funded from cash and borrowings. This is an Analyst Interpretation of capital allocation, not a finding of extraction: the covenant tests are met per the Company, and no related-party leakage or collateral release is documented.

Subsequent events to the cutoff: the fourth quarter dividend declaration of October 28, 2026 is the only post-quarter event in the pack. Nothing dated after October 28, 2026 is supplied, so developments between that date and November 5, 2026 are Insufficient Information.

Nine-month 2026 revenue is above the prior year because the average realised gold price is higher, while gold sold is lower (the release attributes the revenue increase to price, partly offset by volume), and Adjusted EBITDA is also higher. At the same time, cash capital spending, including capitalised interest, exceeds operating cash flow, so cash has fallen and debt has risen, partly through the Foran acquisition (debt assumed) and partly through revolver draws. fields.value: Eldorado's business is a producing gold group with polymetallic by-products, now adding two copper-bearing mines through commissioning at the same time. Revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came mainly from gold, in three geographic segments, with Canada the largest after the Foran acquisition. The operating mines carry the credit today: Lamaque and Olympias improved, while Kisladag and Efemcukuru weakened on lower grades, and cost guidance was raised. The transaction that matters to a creditor is the all-share purchase of Foran, which closed on April 14, 2026: it added McIlvenna Bay and debt assumed of 355,321 (US$ thousand, recorded at fair value), mainly the Sprott facility, which is secured on the acquired assets with a company guarantee, plus an equipment facility. No new notes were issued in the period; new funding was revolver draws, the final overrun draw on the Skouries project loan and the acquired debt. Management describes Skouries as fully funded; that is a management claim, and the pack does not include a funding model. Skouries first concentrate was achieved on September 8, 2026 and McIlvenna Bay first copper concentrate in June 2026, but both commercial production dates are late in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the capital estimates and 2026 production guidance have moved adversely. Ownership, control rights and any shareholder agreements are not disclosed in the pack. Behaviour is assessed on documented actions only: a dividend programme was started and buybacks continued during the build, leadership changed on September 30, 2026, and no priming, drop-down or other creditor-adverse action is documented. Source evidence is primary and dated, so evidence quality is High for filed statements and Medium for management releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one transaction in the period is the acquisition of Foran Mining Corporation, completed on April 14, 2026 by court-approved plan of arrangement. The Q3 statements say the Company acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding common shares of Foran for 0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran share (Q3 statements page:8: "0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran common share"). Total consideration transferred was 2,394,995 (US$ thousand), of which share consideration was 2,385,625, cash 4,154, replacement option value 3,096 and the previously held equity interest 2,120; 64,668,321 shares were issued (Q3 statements pages:8, 17). The principal asset is the McIlvenna Bay project in Saskatchewan. The acquisition was therefore financed with equity, not debt, and the statements show net cash received on acquisition of 159,110 (Q3 statements page:3). Net assets acquired include property, plant and equipment of 2,696,191, goodwill of 446,181, debt assumed of 355,321 and a deferred tax liability of 501,024; the measurement is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year (Q3 statements pages:9, 10). Acquisition-related costs expensed in the nine months were 19.3 million (US$) (Q3 statements page:10). The Q1 statements disclose the completion as an event after the reporting date (Q1 statements page:22).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The debt assumed comprises the Sprott Credit Facility (a fully drawn 250 million non-revolving facility plus 44.9 million capitalised interest, maturing September 30, 2031, floating at 6.95% over the greater of three-month SOFR and 2.00%, secured by the realisable value of the acquired Foran assets and subject to a Company guarantee), the Sandvik Equipment Finance Facility (C$50.1 million outstanding, 60-month repayment) and repayable government contributions (Q3 statements pages:14, 15). Principal repayments on the Sprott facility start on June 30, 2027 at 2.65% of outstanding principal per quarter. Its terms mean the lender has a claim over the acquired assets ahead of unsecured creditors of the group on those assets, and the Company guarantee ties the facility to the parent; the pack does not include the credit agreement, so the full security and guarantee scope is Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new bond or note issue is reported in the period. New borrowing was: draws on the revolving senior secured credit facility totalling 325.0 million in the nine months (225.0 million of it in Q3 2026); the final 60.0 million euro draw on the Skouries Contingent Overrun Facility in Q2 2026; and net proceeds of 2,469 (US$ thousand) from other debt. The revolver was increased from 350 million to 450 million on May 26, 2026 through the accordion, and on August 12, 2026 amended to a 600 million limit with maturity extended to March 1, 2029 and, in the Company's words, improved pricing and covenant terms (Q3 statements page:14: "enhancing financial flexibility through improved pricing and covenant terms"). The amended covenant terms are not stated beyond the interest cover and net leverage levels in the note, so what changed is Insufficient Information. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Eldorado Gold's credit view is cautiously constructive: profitable mines at high gold prices support debt, but debt is rising and cash falling while two new mines are commissioned. The strongest support is operating earnings and low illustrative leverage, financed partly by shares issued for Foran. The weakest point is nine-month free cash flow of USD negative 654.3 million and liquidity down from USD 976.0 million to USD 671.5 million since December 2025. The outcome depends on Skouries and McIlvenna Bay reaching commercial production in late Q4 2026 at or near the revised budgets, on gold prices holding, and on the senior notes and revolver refinancing from 2029. Confidence is Medium because trailing earnings and covenant headroom are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Eldorado Gold's cash is being consumed by growth spending rather than by operations. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 it generated USD 425.7 million of operating cash flow from continuing operations but spent USD 1,210.0 million on property, plant and equipment and USD 45.9 million on capitalised interest paid, a shortfall of about USD 830.2 million before acquisition cash, dividends, buybacks and borrowings (CP-1, Calculations). Company-defined free cash flow was negative USD 654.3 million; excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay it was positive USD 202.1 million (Q3 release page:13). Mechanic: the operating mines are cash generative and the two projects absorb it, so default risk is driven by project completion, not by the operating base. Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Liquidity has fallen but covers near-term maturities. Unrestricted cash was USD 396.8 million and the undrawn revolver USD 274.7 million at September 30, 2026, together USD 671.5 million against USD 976.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1). Principal falling due within a year is USD 141.1 million, so liquidity is about 4.8 times that amount (Calculations). Restricted cash of USD 71.9 million for the Skouries term loan reserve and the undrawn euro 30 million VAT facility are excluded. Mechanic: the cushion is adequate for scheduled repayments but not for a prolonged slip in the start-ups combined with a lower gold price. Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Debt rose by USD 710.4 million to USD 1,985.4 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (carrying amount). The increase came from USD 321.6 million of revolver borrowings, USD 68.1 million from the final overrun draw on the Skouries loan, and USD 350.5 million of Foran-related debt (the Sprott facility net of its redemption option derivative asset, the equipment facility and government contributions), partly offset by repayments and movements on the Skouries project loans and the VAT facility (CP-1 debt table; Calculations). Foran itself was paid for with shares (USD 2,385.6 million of share consideration), which kept the acquisition from adding to leverage through the purchase price (CP-1A). Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Reported leverage looks moderate only on an illustrative basis. Total debt to annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is 1.67 times and net debt to the same measure 1.34 times; neither is a trailing twelve-month figure because FY2025 EBITDA is not supplied, and the base includes Foran only from April 14, 2026 and no Skouries contribution (CP-1). Cash interest cover (Adjusted EBITDA over interest paid plus capitalised interest paid) was 11.96 times for nine months 2026 and 9.81 times for Q3 2026. These do not use the covenant definitions, so headroom against the revolver tests of at least 3.00 times interest cover and at most 3.50 times net leverage is Not calculable. The illustrative figures sit well inside those levels, which is a reading and not a compliance finding; the Company states it complied at September 30, 2026 (Q3 statements page:14). Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Skouries and McIlvenna Bay execution is the pivotal risk. First concentrate was reached at Skouries on September 8, 2026 and at McIlvenna Bay in June 2026, with commercial production for both expected late in Q4 2026 (CP-1A). The Skouries project capital estimate rose from about USD 1.315 billion in the Q1 release to about USD 1.425 billion, the McIlvenna Bay estimate from USD 952 million in the Q2 release to USD 975 million, and the 2026 production outlook was cut to 425,000 to 475,000 ounces from 495,000 to 600,000 ounces. On the release's own figures, remaining Skouries project capital is about USD 46 million and accelerated operational capital about USD 104 million, with up to USD 30 million more possible (Calculations); the remaining McIlvenna Bay spend is Not calculable because spending before the acquisition date is not in the pack. Mechanic: further slippage extends the period of negative free cash flow and delays the debt reduction that management says it expects. Management Language on funding ("fully funded") is not adopted because no funding model is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Refinancing is concentrated and amortisation starts soon. Principal due by year after September 30, 2026 is USD 141.1 million, 142.5 million, 958.8 million, 162.4 million, 354.7 million and 258.2 million beyond year five (CP-1). The third year contains the USD 500.0 million 6.25% senior notes due September 1, 2029 and the USD 325.0 million revolver drawn to March 1, 2029, the largest bucket by a wide margin. The Skouries term loan, non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries and Hellas Gold assets, begins repaying on December 31, 2026 in 13 semi-annual instalments (Q3 statements page:13). Mechanic: if the start-ups deliver, cash flow and the equity-funded balance sheet should support refinancing; if not, the 2029 wall arrives with higher debt. Documentary Fact for the schedule, Analyst Interpretation for the refinancing reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Shareholder returns continued during the build. Dividends of USD 54.1 million and cancelled buybacks of USD 83.9 million in nine months 2026, about USD 138.0 million together, were paid while free cash flow was negative (CP-1A, Calculations). The senior notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances and the Company reports compliance. No creditor-adverse action is documented. Mechanic: these returns draw on the same liquidity that funds the projects and can be reduced by the board; they are a monitoring point, not a finding of extraction. Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Earnings quality needs care. Net earnings from continuing operations were USD 426.2 million for nine months 2026 against USD 270.0 million a year earlier, but the 2025 period included a deferred tax recovery of USD 89.4 million and the 2026 effective tax rate was 37.6% against 16.8% (CP-1 Calculations). The Adjusted EBITDA measure of USD 892.0 million adds back a USD 97.6 million realised loss on gold and copper derivatives and USD 21.3 million of acquisition costs, and removes a USD 100.6 million unrealised derivative gain (Q3 release page:24). Mechanic: the realised swap loss is a real cost of the Skouries financing hedges that the adjusted figure leaves out; those swaps have expired with financial settlement (Q3 statements page:22), so the item should not recur, but the adjusted measure is higher than the unadjusted result for 2026. Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, the operating base earns at high gold prices: the average realised gold price was USD 4,326 per ounce in Q3 2026 against USD 3,527 a year earlier, and Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 892.0 million against USD 571.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1). Second, diversification across Turkiye, Canada and Greece with Canada now the largest segment at about 45% of nine-month revenue, and several mines at different cost levels, with Lamaque cash costs of USD 897 per ounce in Q3 2026 (CP-1A, Calculations; Analyst Interpretation). Third, an equity-funded Foran purchase that added roughly 24.7% to shares outstanding rather than debt to fund the price, and an extended and enlarged revolver of USD 600.0 million maturing March 1, 2029 (Documentary Fact). Fourth, a Skouries project loan that the notes describe as non-recourse to Eldorado Gold Corporation, which limits parent exposure to that lender if the project falls short (Documentary Fact for the description; the legal documents are not supplied, so the extent of recourse is not verified). Fifth, interest cover on cash interest of about ten to twelve times on matched bases (Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, negative free cash flow and falling liquidity, with debt up USD 710.4 million in nine months (Documentary Fact). Second, cost and guidance deterioration: all-in sustaining cost guidance raised and 2026 production outlook cut, with Kisladag and Olympias weaker (Documentary Fact). Third, start-up risk and rising project capital at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, with commercial production dates still forward-looking (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Fourth, a concentrated maturity profile and the start of Skouries term loan repayments in December 2026 (Documentary Fact). Fifth, a leadership transition on September 30, 2026 during the overrun period and shareholder distributions during the build (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the credit effect). Sixth, high effective tax in 2026 and exposure to a high gold price: the earnings strength depends on a gold price the company does not control, and the pack contains no sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation; sensitivity Not supplied).
